title: Sundown

wikipedia.about: Gordon Lightfoot's 1974 song Sundown, title track of his album Sundown
facts: Single issued 25 March 1974 on Reprise, written by Lightfoot and produced by Lenny Waronker.
Recorded in November 1973 at Eastern Sound in Toronto; Red Shea played electric lead guitar.
Reached number one on the US Hot 100 and Easy Listening charts, and also topped the Canadian chart; his only Hot 100 number one.
Certified Gold by the RIAA for a million units shipped.
Lightfoot said in 2008 the lyrics came from wondering what his girlfriend was doing out with friends while he wrote at home; often linked to Cathy Smith.
Covered by Deryl Dodd (1999) and Elwood (2000), both minor chart entries.
Canadian singer-songwriter born 17 November 1938 in Orillia, Ontario; died 1 May 2023 aged 84.
Credited with helping define the 1970s singer-songwriter era and considered among Canada's most influential songwriters.
His biographer Nicholas Jennings summed up his subjects as trains, shipwrecks, rivers, highways, lovers and loneliness.

results.title: The Story Behind the Song: Sundown by Gordon Lightfoot

The album hit number one in the US and Canada, staying top in Canada for five straight weeks.
Despite its mellow sound the song is described as dark, expressing jealousy and paranoia.
Lightfoot said it concerned his roughly three-year relationship with Cathy Smith, not his ex-wife.
He said he wrote it around sunset at a farm he rented as a writing retreat.

title: Any Other Name

wikipedia.about: The 1999 American Beauty soundtrack album, which includes a Thomas Newman track called Any Other Name.
facts: The album was released on October 5, 1999 by DreamWorks Records and has 13 tracks.
Two tracks come from Thomas Newman's film score; the full score was released separately in 2000.
The album was nominated for a 2000 Grammy for Best Compilation Soundtrack.
Jakatta sampled Newman's Any Other Name for his 2000 house track American Dream.
